englishTranslation: Beef dipped in vinegar hot pot
atAGlance: Bò nhúng dấm is thin beef slices swished through hot vinegar broth, usually with onion, herbs, rice paper, and a small sharp dip of fish sauce, chili, or lime-pepper salt.
whatItIs: Bò nhúng dấm is thin beef swished through hot vinegar broth, then rolled with rice paper, herbs, noodles, and a fish-sauce-lime dip. It is a table-cooking, roll-your-own meal.
howToEnjoy: Swish beef briefly in the vinegar broth, lay it into rice paper with herbs and noodles, roll, then dip. Keep the beef tender by not overcooking it.
howLocalsOrder: Order bò nhúng dấm by table size and ask about rice paper, herbs, noodles, and the fish-sauce-lime dip before everyone starts rolling.
worthKnowing: The vinegar broth cooks and brightens the beef; the rice paper and herbs turn it into a fresh roll rather than a plain hot pot.
goodToKnow: Swish the beef briefly so it stays tender, then roll it with herbs and noodles. This is a table-size meal, so order for the group rather than one quick bowl.

orderLine.vietnamese: Cho tôi một phần bò nhúng dấm.
orderLine.english: I’d like one order of beef dipped in vinegar hot pot.
